validity.recommendation: No structural action needed. Keep status=operating, StartYear1=2003, Operator/Owner=Kinder Morgan. See the separate spec concern for Capacity/LengthKnown staleness and the Location caveat below.
validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: real, well-documented. Independently confirmed by Oil & Gas Journal (2003-03-26, 'Kinder Morgan Energy Partners LP has placed into service its Mier-Monterrey natural gas pipeline that stretches from south Texas to Monterrey... The 95 mile pipeline interconnects with the southern end of Kinder Morgan's Texas intrastate system in Starr County, Tex. Pemex Gas Y Petroquimica Basica (PGPB) has subscribed for the entire capacity of 375 MMcfd... came on line Mar. 20 [2003]'), by North American Oil & Gas Pipelines (napipelines.com, 2015-07-29, via Wayback since the live domain no longer resolves: 'Kinder Morgan Gas Natural de Mexico S. de R.L. de C.V. owns and operates the 85-mile Mier-Monterrey pipeline, which has been in service since 2003...'), by Kinder Morgan's own current live operations page (kindermorgan.com), and by a Mexican regulatory filing: KMGNM's CRE-mandated Open Season Procedure dated 2020-06-12 (45pp PDF) operating under Permiso de Transporte de Gas Natural No. G/003/TRA/96, which gives the exact border-crossing coordinates near Ciudad Mier, Tamaulipas and the CENAGAS/SISTRANGAS interconnection at Apodaca, Nuevo Leon. This is a real, currently-operating cross-border pipeline, not a GEM-only entity.
CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified as a gas transmission pipeline (GGIT). It is an international interstate/cross-border trunk line connecting the Kinder Morgan Texas intrastate system to Mexico's SISTRANGAS national grid and to a 1,000 MW power-plant complex -- not a gathering/feeder line. Fuel=Gas is trivially correct across every source.
DUPLICATE CHECK vs the 45-row roster: no match. The only other Texas-Mexico gas lines on the roster are P0224 NET Mexico (Nueces County -> border, a different corridor, confirmed distinct by kindermorgan.com's own page listing NET Mexico and Mier-Monterrey as separate systems) and P0290 Nueva Era (Webb County -> Escobedo, NL -- also confirmed as a separate system by the El Economista 2018 article, which explicitly distinguishes the Nueva Era system 'que viene desde Webb County' from the Mier-Monterrey system it is discussing). Starr County (Mier-Monterrey) and Webb County (Nueva Era) are different border crossings; no overlap.
ATTRIBUTION: Operator 'Kinder Morgan Gas Natural de Mexico' and Owner1 'Kinder Morgan' 100% are corroborated (see Operator/Owner fills below). LOCATION CAVEAT: GEM's EndLocation is 'Monterrey,' which matches the boilerplate description used verbatim by both kindermorgan.com and napipelines.com ('...to Monterrey, Mexico') -- but the CRE open-season filing is more precise: the pipeline physically terminates at the KMGNM 'Cabezal M1' header in the municipality of APODACA, Nuevo Leon (coordinates given), which interconnects to SISTRANGAS there. Apodaca is part of Greater Monterrey metro, so 'Monterrey' is a defensible shorthand used by all press coverage, not an error worth changing -- flagging only as a precision note, not a location concern.
COVERAGE: opened 8 of the 9 harvested wiki citations. The Reuters 2013 URL (idUSL1N0BYHGY20130306) returned HTTP 401 (paywall/block) and has no Wayback capture available (CDX query returned no snapshots) -- access failure, not evidence of deletion, left uncited. The Kinder Morgan pipeportal.kindermorgan.com nomination-portal page was opened and verifies live but is a JS-driven scheduling portal with no static numeric content usable as a citation; not relied on for any value.

validity.recommendation: Route to Update: verify whether Capacity should move from 640 to ~675 MMcf/d (and LengthKnown from 90 to ~86 mi) to reflect the operator's more recently dated system description; do not apply blind.
validity.researcher_notes:
Capacity and LengthKnown are internally inconsistent across the operator's OWN documents, not just across independent press. Two facts anchor a timeline: (1) the 2020-06-12 CRE Open Season Procedure PDF (KMMX_Open_Season_Guideline.pdf) states KMGNM plans to add new capacity of up to 35,000 MMBtu/d via compression, subject to CRE authorization of a permit modification to G/003/TRA/96; (2) KMGNM's own Spanish-language system-overview PDF (KMMX_Cpny_Overview.pdf, Word/PDF metadata CreationDate 2021-08-18) states the pipeline 'actualmente' extends 86 miles (139 km) and has a capacity of 675,000 MMBtu/d. 640,000 + 35,000 = 675,000 exactly -- i.e., the Aug-2021 PDF reads as the post-expansion figure, while GEM's current Capacity=640.00 matches kindermorgan.com's English operations page verbatim ('90-mile... capacity to transport 640,000 MMBtu per day... currently being evaluated for further expansion'), which is undated and appears to predate the 2020-2021 compression addition -- i.e. stale relative to KMGNM's own newer document.
LENGTH shows the same pattern plus real historical variance: OGJ (at 2003 commissioning) said 95 miles; napipelines (2015) said 85 miles; kindermorgan.com (undated) says 90 miles (= GEM's exact value); the Aug-2021 KMGNM PDF says 86 miles. All four cluster in an 85-95 mile band -- not wildly divergent, consistent with routine pipeline-mileage reporting variance across different vintages/surveys -- but none independently pins GEM's precise '90.00' figure, and the operator's own newest document says 86.
An independent 2015 data point corroborates the PRE-2020-expansion capacity band: BNamericas (syndicated via Yahoo Finanzas, 2015) states the line 'tiene una capacidad de 18.1Mm3/d' -- 18.1 million m3/day x 35.3147 ft3/m3 = ~639 MMcf/d, matching GEM's 640 almost exactly, which is a genuinely independent (non-KMGNM) source for the PRE-expansion figure. So GEM's current 640/90 values are well-supported for a ~2015-2020 snapshot, but the operator's own newer document suggests the true CURRENT figures are closer to 675 MMcf/d and 86 mi following the CRE-authorized compression addition. Not applying this myself -- it is a genuine value judgment (has the 35,000 MMBtu/d addition actually gone into service yet?) that belongs with Update, not silently overwritten here.
Note on the two PDF citations: automatic url_verifier substring-matching FAILS on both (200 OK, but the expected tokens are inside compressed PDF content streams the naive checker cannot see -- an acknowledged verifier limitation per its own docstring). Content was independently confirmed via `pdftotext -layout` (both extract to complete, on-topic Spanish text; see notes above for exact quoted figures) before being cited here.

Independently corroborated by El Economista (2018-07-22), which quotes CENAGAS director general David Madero Suarez discussing the pipeline's current (as of mid-2018) throughput and expansion plans -- an independent third-party (Mexican federal gas-control regulator official), not Kinder Morgan.

Natural gas pipeline ('natural gas pipeline' / 'Gasoducto de Gas Natural') throughout every source consulted (OGJ, napipelines, El Economista, kindermorgan.com, the CRE filings). Trivial but unanimous.

Oil & Gas Journal, dateline 2003-03-26: pipeline 'came on line Mar. 20' [2003], an $87 million project. North American Oil & Gas Pipelines (2015-07-29, via Wayback -- live domain no longer resolves): 'has been in service since 2003.' Two independent trade-press origins, 12 years apart, agree exactly.

kindermorgan.com's own current operations page states '640,000 MMBtu per day.' Independently, BNamericas (syndicated via Yahoo Finanzas, 2015) states capacity of '18.1Mm3/d' = ~639 MMcf/d (18.1 x 35.3147), matching to within rounding. IMPORTANT: see the paired spec concern above -- a more recently dated Kinder Morgan document (Aug 2021) reports 675,000 MMBtu/d, 640k+35k(from the 2020 CRE compression-expansion filing)=675k exactly, suggesting 640 may now be stale. Refs here support GEM's EXISTING value as of its apparent ~2015-2020 vintage; the possible newer figure is flagged separately, not applied.

kindermorgan.com's own current operations page states '90-mile Mier-Monterrey Pipeline,' matching GEM's LengthKnown exactly -- but this is a single operator source. Other vintages cluster nearby without matching exactly: OGJ 2003 says 95 mile (at commissioning), napipelines 2015 says 85-mile, and KMGNM's own Aug-2021 PDF says 86 miles (139 km). See the paired spec concern above for the full range and the likely explanation (as-built vs. later compression/looping additions changing effective route length reporting).

kindermorgan.com and napipelines.com use near-identical phrasing ('stretches/stretching from the International Border between the United States and Mexico in Starr County, Texas, to Monterrey, Mexico'), which reads as company boilerplate picked up by the trade press rather than two independently-derived descriptions -- so treated as one origin, tier medium. A precision caveat, not a location error: KMGNM's 2020 CRE Open Season filing gives the actual physical terminus as the 'Cabezal M1' header in the municipality of APODACA, Nuevo Leon (with coordinates), not literally Monterrey proper -- Apodaca is part of Greater Monterrey metro, so GEM's 'Monterrey' is defensible shorthand used by every press source, not flagged as a concern.
